one_liner: Fairfax County outreach role that persuades employers and commuters to adopt carpooling, transit, telework and other Transportation Demand Management programs to reduce driving.
fit_summary: The core of this job is outreach, sales engagement and relationship-building with employers and regional partners, which matches Daniel's outgoing, people-oriented strengths and public-policy knowledge. Consulting work for government clients at IEM supports stakeholder and program-implementation framing. The gap is transportation-specific planning experience and possibly a planning-related degree, which the truncated posting does not show.
eligibility: Open the full posting and confirm the employment standards for Transportation Planner II. County planner classes often list a specific degree and years of experience, and the excerpt does not show them.
Check whether a driver's license is required; outreach roles that visit employer sites commonly need one.
Confirm any preferred qualifications, such as TDM, commuter services or sales experience, listed in the full posting.
No federal status, clearance or residency requirement appears in the excerpt, but verify in the full posting.
strategy: Apply on governmentjobs.com between October 17 and November 12, 2026. Submit early, because Fairfax County may close or screen applications as they arrive.

Frame your IEM work as stakeholder engagement and program implementation for government clients, such as coordinating with agencies, briefing partners or supporting outreach. Use your actual duties and titles.
Lead with relationship-building, public-facing communication and persuasion, since the posting explicitly calls for outreach and sales engagement.

Learn the basics of TDM before you apply: Fairfax Connector, Commuter Connections, vanpool incentives, telework programs and Virginia's commuter benefit programs. Mention them knowledgeably in your supplemental answers.
Complete the county application and supplemental questions in full detail rather than writing 'see resume.' County HR often scores the application itself.
Tie your policy knowledge to regional transportation goals, such as reducing congestion and supporting air quality, and to working with county leadership priorities.
resume_bullets: Built and maintained relationships with [number/type] government client stakeholders at IEM, coordinating [meetings/briefings/deliverables] to support [emergency management or recovery program].
Conducted outreach to [audience] to promote participation in [program], using [presentations/events/email campaigns] and resulting in [result, if known].
Translated complex [policy/program] information into clear materials for [public/officials/partners], supporting [outcome].
interview_questions: How would you approach a large employer that has no interest in commuter programs?
Tell us about a time you built a partnership with an external organization from scratch.
What do you know about Transportation Demand Management, and why does it matter for Fairfax County?
How would you track and report the success of your outreach efforts?
watch_outs: The posting excerpt is truncated, so verify any degree or planning-experience requirement for Planner II before you invest time.
The role is not remote, and site visits to employers may require local travel and a valid driver's license.
Pay offers often start near the bottom of the range for candidates without direct transportation experience.
